entries.description: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) is a protective filter that lines the brain's blood vessels and is notoriously hard to penetrate, making the treatment of brain disorders very difficult. Strategies designed to breach the BBB include using brain surgery and focused ultrasound waves to create physical openings for the transportation of medicines and employing engineered adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) to ferry genetic payloads into desired locations, but these methods have limitations. entries.title: [Articles] Belzutifan plus lenvatinib versus cabozantinib in patients with previously treated advanced renal cell carcinoma (LITESPARK-011): an open-label, randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial
entries.description: Belzutifan–lenvatinib represents a novel and efficacious treatment option. Although overall survival was not significantly different between the groups, belzutifan–lenvatinib might be a new standard of care for patients with advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma with disease progression after previous anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy. The safety profile of belzutifan–lenvatinib was consistent with those of the individual drugs.

entries.title: [Articles] Switch to once-weekly, single-tablet islatravir–lenacapavir from daily standard of care for HIV-1 (ISLEND-2): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, active-controlled, phase 3 non-inferiority trial
entries.description: Once-weekly islatravir–lenacapavir showed non-inferior efficacy to the standard of care and was generally well tolerated. Longer-term safety data will provide further valuable insights beyond the week 48 data presented here. Islatravir–lenacapavir has potential to be the first once-weekly complete oral single-tablet regimen for HIV-1 treatment.

entries.title: [Articles] Multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting via small thoracotomy versus sternotomy (MIST): an investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomised controlled trial
entries.description: For selected patients with multivessel coronary artery disease, MICS CABG performed by experienced teams improved patient-reported physical recovery at 1 month compared with sternotomy CABG, with no apparent safety penalty through to 12 months. These findings support consideration of MICS CABG in appropriately selected patients treated by experienced teams, and further studies of implementation, recovery pathways, and long-term outcomes.

entries.title: WHO: Integration, innovation and community leadership key to ending HIV, hepatitis and STIs
entries.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) today launched a new report assessing progress in implementing the Global Health Sector Strategies (GHSS) on HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) for 2022–2030. Released during the 26th International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2026) and ahead of World Hepatitis Day (28 July), the report highlights significant achievements and persistent challenges in the global response to these epidemics.

entries.title: WHO launches seven strategies to prevent drowning
entries.description: Ahead of World Drowning Prevention Day on 25 July, the World Health Organization (WHO) is launching a new technical package to help governments and communities implement seven proven measures to reduce drowning deaths.

entries.title: [Articles] High-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous stem-cell transplantation versus non-myeloablative consolidation in primary CNS lymphoma (MATRix/IELSG43): a randomised phase 3 trial
entries.description: In the largest randomised trial in untreated PCNSL to date, HCT–ASCT significantly improved progression-free and overall survival compared with non-myeloablative consolidation in patients who had completed induction treatment, establishing it as the preferred consolidation strategy in fit patients.

entries.title: UN report: Global hunger levels ease for third consecutive year as regional disparities persist
entries.description: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025, demonstrating that progress is possible. entries.title: More health workers, stronger systems: Africa’s new ambitious goal
entries.description: Facing a projected shortage of more than six million health professionals by 2035, African countries are stepping up efforts to strengthen their workforce, with a new decade-long plan announced on Wednesday during a meeting of health ministers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

entries.description: Results may be months away, but efforts are advancing towards enhanced treatment and the world’s first vaccine for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday as deaths and cases rise in the largest ever outbreak on record in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

entries.title: High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution
entries.description: The AIDS epidemic could stage a comeback amid unequal access to breakthrough prevention medicines and a sharp decline in global funding, according to a UN report released on Monday ahead of the opening of the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

entries.title: WHO marks 25 years of Research4Life, advancing access to scientific knowledge in more than 120 countries
entries.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) today marks the 25th anniversary of Research4Life, a public-private partnership that provides researchers, educators, health professionals and policy-makers in low- and middle-income countries with affordable or free access to scientific knowledge. entries.description: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are tracking a growing share of people exposed to Ebola, but the epidemic in the country's restive east continues to outpace their ability to find and isolate the sick, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

entries.description: An expert in machine learning, statistics, and computation, Rakhlin succeeds Professor Ankur Moitra.

entries.description: As a first-generation student from a small town, Gohar Khan ’21 had to navigate the college admissions process largely on his own. entries.title: Australia’s red soil may be hiding a massive clean energy source
entries.description: Researchers have discovered that Western Australia’s iron-rich rocks can naturally generate hydrogen and that the process may be boosted to produce much larger amounts. If it can be scaled up, the vast formations beneath the Pilbara could become a major new source of low-emission energy for Australia and potentially the world.

entries.title: Youth advocates gather in New York to launch new AI standards
entries.description: As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms everything from how we learn, to the job market, children are adopting the technology more than three times faster than adults – exposing them to unique opportunities and risks.

entries.title: Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches among new World Heritage Sites
entries.description: From the peaks of Mount Olympus in Greece to the shores of the “D-Day” beaches in France, 25 cultural or natural landmarks from across the globe have been newly inscribed on the World Heritage List, updated annually by the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).

entries.title: UN calls for urgent action to protect children from online information risks
entries.description: More than eight in 10 young people aged 15 to 24 worldwide are now online, and in low-income countries they outpace the rest of the population nearly two to one.

entries.title: ADB Approves $400 Million Financing Facility to Modernize Borders, Facilitate Trade in CAREC Region
entries.description: ADB has approved a $400 million regional financing facility to modernize border crossing points, lower transport and logistics costs, and improve the movement of people and goods across the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) region.

entries.title: ADB and Partners Launch Initiative to Scale Financing for Land Degradation and Desertification in Asia and the Pacific
entries.description: ADB has launched together with partners the Financing Investments and Eradicating Land Degradation and Desertification Initiative, a regional partnership to attract at least $2 billion by 2035 to invest in programs that restore lands and strengthen drought resilience across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB Approves Project to Expand Access to Life-Saving Care in Mongolia’s Provinces
entries.description: ADB has approved a $225 million loan—its largest health sector investment in Mongolia—to expand access to quality health care across the country’s provinces through major upgrades in health infrastructure, emergency care, digital health systems, medical equipment, and workforce capacity.

entries.title: ADB, FSM Development Bank to Support Women Entrepreneurs in the Federated States of Micronesia
entries.description: ADB has signed a $5 million financing package with Federated States of Micronesia Development Bank (FSMDB) to expand access to finance for women-led small and medium-sized enterprises in the Federated States of Micronesia.

entries.title: ADB Approves $1 Billion Loan to Support Sustainable Growth and Resilience of India’s Cities
entries.description: ADB has approved a $1 billion loan to support the Government of India’s urban reform agenda by maintaining momentum of investment and reforms aimed at transforming cities into engines of economic growth, innovation, and livability.

entries.title: ADB’s Private Sector Operations Drive Development Impact with Strong Growth
entries.description: ADB's private sector financing increased by 38% in 2025 to $9.5 billion, including $900 million in long-term direct mobilization for transaction advisory services, according to the Private Sector Operations in 2025 Report on Development Effectiveness.

entries.title: ADB Launches Fund to Scale Resilient Agribusiness and Sustainable Rangeland Management in Mongolia
entries.description: ADB has launched the Green Inclusive Regional Agribusiness Fund to expand access to finance for herders, cooperatives, small and medium-sized enterprises, and agribusinesses investing in sustainable livestock value chains in Mongolia.

entries.title: ADB Supports Tbilisi Bypass with $250 Million Loan to Boost Georgia’s Regional Connectivity
entries.description: ADB has approved a $250 million loan to help build a critical bypass around Tbilisi that will improve road connectivity, ease congestion, and strengthen Georgia’s role as a regional transport hub in the region.

entries.title: ADB to Deploy $450 Million to Shield Cambodia, Sri Lanka from Middle East Impact
entries.description: ADB is set to deploy $450 million to protect poor households and strengthen the economies of Cambodia and Sri Lanka as the conflict in the Middle East drives up costs and deepens uncertainty across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB Approves $850 Million Loan to Accelerate Affordable Rooftop Solar Adoption for Households in India
entries.description: ADB has approved an $850 million loan to support reforms that will speed up the rollout of the Government of India’s flagship rooftop solar program, boosting the resilience of Indian households through better access to affordable clean energy, mobilizing private sector investment, and strengthening the skills of grid personnel and rural entrepreneurs.

entries.title: ADB, Japan Establish New Water Security Fund
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Japan established a new fund to strengthen water security and protect people across Asia and the Pacific from worsening floods, droughts, and other water-related shocks. Japan will make an initial $10 million contribution to the fund.

entries.title: The rise of electoral democracy
entries.description: How elections spread, voting rights expanded, and political competition developed around the world over the last two centuries.

entries.title: After post-pandemic improvement, youth unemployment is rising again
entries.description: Frustrated by skyrocketing youth unemployment, among other issues, tens of thousands of Gen Z activists took to the streets of Nepal last year, demanding a stake in the country’s economic growth. The protest worked and the prime minister resigned.

entries.title: Global hunger declines again but progress remains uneven across regions
entries.description: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025 showing that progress is possible, but gains remain fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by the 2030 deadline.

entries.title: ADB Accelerates Disaster Response and Recovery for Vanuatu
entries.description: ADB has approved the first project under its region-wide crisis financing mechanism, giving Vanuatu faster access to financing after disasters and other major emergencies. The financing can be used to support families, deliver essential supplies and equipment, and repair damaged public services and infrastructure.

entries.title: ADB Sells $2 Billion 10-Year Global Benchmark Bond
entries.description: ADB has priced a $2 billion 10-year global bond, proceeds of which will become part of ADB’s ordinary capital resources.

entries.title: ADB Puts Team on the Ground in Türkiye as Financing Demand Surges
entries.description: Recognizing Türkiye’s growing regional importance, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) will establish an office in the country as it prepares to commit about $3 billion a year to earthquake recovery, critical infrastructure, businesses, and trade routes linking Asia and Europe.

entries.title: ADB Loan Supports Stronger Earthquake Resilience at Schools in Armenia
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Armenia have signed a $293 million loan agreement to expand resilient, inclusive school infrastructure nationwide and strengthen the country's capacity to manage earthquake risks.

entries.title: ADB President Urges Faster Action on Water Security
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda has called for faster investment and reform to secure water across Asia and the Pacific, pointing to a new ADB-administered fund with Japan that will help developing economies strengthen disaster preparedness, infrastructure, and water management.

entries.title: ADB Launches Initiative to Bring Japanese Startup Innovation to Southeast Asia and the Pacific
entries.description: ADB and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have launched the Southeast Asia Emerging Entrepreneurs Kickstart initiative to help promising startups scale solutions to complex development challenges in Southeast Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: New initiative launched to shield terrorism victims from online harm
entries.description: The UN has launched a new initiative to protect victims of terrorist attacks from online harm and re-traumatisation, drawing on harrowing survivor accounts, from the Nova Music Festival in Israel to an attack on a FIFA World Cup final viewing party in Uganda.

entries.title: Aid reaches hundreds of thousands in Gaza amid severe food insecurity
entries.description: As hunger deepens across Gaza, humanitarian agencies continue to deliver food and other essential supplies to families in need.

entries.title: Explainer: UN peace operations work to create, preserve peace
entries.description: Supporting the first democratic elections after brutal civil wars in Mozambique and Cambodia. Disarming thousands of child soldiers in Sierra Leone. Helping to secure Namibia’s independence from South Africa. These are some of the contributions of UN operations around the world to help countries transition from conflict to lasting peace.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: Drone strikes and political impasse in Libya
entries.description: As Libya faces a political impasse delaying long-planned elections alongside clashes and drone strikes that left a major oil refinery ablaze, the Security Council heard the latest updates, with an activist warning that the collision of extreme heat, water scarcity and environmental shocks with political division, armed insecurity and struggling institutions clearly makes the situation a peace and security issue. UN News app users can follow our live coverage here.

entries.title: Gaza: Destruction of buildings rises by nearly 10 per cent since ceasefire
entries.description: New satellite assessments show the destruction of buildings in Gaza has climbed by nearly 10 per cent since October’s faltering ceasefire between Hamas and Israeli forces aim to end the two-year war, which reduced cities to rubble and displaced more than one million people, UN agencies said on Thursday.

entries.title: Lebanon: UN peacekeepers count hundreds of Israeli strikes and incursions in a single weekend
entries.description: Israeli forces fired 455 projectiles into south Lebanon and breached Lebanese airspace 97 times between Friday and Sunday, the UN's peacekeeping mission in the country reported Monday – among the heaviest fire seen in months.

entries.title: Fighting deepens needs and fuels further displacement in Sudan
entries.description: Ongoing conflict, displacement and funding shortages continue to deepen needs in Sudan, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Monday, underscoring the need for greater civilian protection.

entries.title: Security Council LIVE: Warnings of famine and collapse as South Sudan's peace deal frays
entries.description: Nearly eight million people in South Sudan – more than half the population – face crisis-level hunger, with famine risk now flagged in four counties, as the Security Council met this morning in New York. A cholera outbreak has killed more than 1,700 people, and some aid workers are being killed and abducted even as they try to reach those most at risk. Follow live coverage below.

entries.title: 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test
entries.description: As the world marks the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has launched a global campaign urging governments, organizations and individuals to renew their commitment to protecting people forced to flee war, violence and persecution.

entries.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
entries.description: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country.

entries.description: The final two of ESA's pioneering Cluster spacecraft, Samba and Tango, will end their journeys as they burn up in our atmosphere on 31 August and 1 September respectively. Their targeted reentries mark the end of a mission that has transformed our understanding of Earth's magnetic environment. The final moments also offer a rare scientific opportunity for reentry observations from a plane.
